observations.element: Orders grid + filters (date range, Store, TIB Status, search by order name)
observations.observed_result: Default date range 'Aug 14 - Sep 13', Store 'Any', TIB Status 'Any'. Backed by GET /api/orders?by_teeinblue=1&cursor=&per_page=25&sort=created_at&sort_type=desc. Grid columns: checkbox, Order (links to /orders/{id}), Domain, Store ID (links to Shopify admin order), Date, Total, TIB Status, Store Status, Action. Search-by-name searches the internal order 'name' (e.g. '#1002'), NOT the Shopify checkout confirmation code (e.g. 'JTEL87JY0') — searching by confirmation code returned no results even for a synced order, confirming these are different identifier namespaces.

Shows internal order name + id as '#1002 (#-4322)', TIB status badge 'ready', created timestamp 'Sun, 13 Sep, 2026 04:46:43' (portal renders in America/New_York, 4hr behind the UTC checkout timestamp).

observations.element: Order Items section — one line item card
observations.observed_result: Card shows: 'Campaign by Product Base' type tag; Item ID '#-6957' with its own status badge 'Ready' (distinct from order-level 'ready'); 'Item Activity logs' button; Campaign link (#-2595, 'QA Explore Campaign PB 01'); Title; Variant link (#-88596, 'Vertical Framed Poster / Black / 12in x 18in'); Shopify SKU 'lin_2595_88596'; Fulfilled SKU '65402' (a DIFFERENT sku used for the POD/fulfillment side vs the Shopify-facing SKU); POD service 'Printify'; Shopify fulfillment status (empty); Shopify fulfillment service 'manual'; Price set '55.99 x 1'; Sub total '55.99'; Customization block with 'View customization'/'Edit customization' buttons; Designs section showing the generated mockup image, artwork name, printarea ('front', 12x18), and pixel size (3600x5400) — i.e. the print-ready raster size, much higher resolution than the on-screen preview.

Opens a dialog titled 'Line item #6957 (order )' listing a chronological log for THIS line item, oldest last: (1) 'Line item has been created' 04:48:48; (2) 'Line item is generating a design' 04:48:48 (same second — synchronous kickoff); (3) 'Line item has generated a new design' 04:48:48... wait actually 04:49:08, with details Printarea 13936 / Artwork 4081 / Artwork Version 10953 / Design URL; (4) 'Line item marked as Ready to fulfill' 04:49:10. All 4 events happened automatically within ~22 seconds of order creation, with NO manual action from the merchant side (no fulfill click yet at that point) — design generation and 'Ready' status are fully automatic post-order-creation, not something the merchant triggers.

observations.element: 'Notes', 'Fulfillment Shipping method', 'Customer', 'Shipping address', 'Billing address' side panels
observations.observed_result: Notes: 'No notes from customer'. Fulfillment Shipping method: 'No shipping method' with an 'Edit' button and a 'Set up shipping method' help-doc link — implying shipping method is a SEPARATE, order/instance-level configuration from Shopify's own shipping method chosen at checkout ('Standard' $8.00), required specifically for the fulfillment/POD side. Customer/Shipping/Billing sections mirror exactly what was entered at Shopify checkout (name, email, address) with an 'Edit' affordance on Customer.

observations.element: 'Confirm & Send to fulfill' button (top of Order Items section)
observations.observed_result: Clicking it (user-performed, per explicit authorization — this is a real production/billing-adjacent action) opens a review dialog (NOT an immediate submit) titled '#1002' with a 'View order details' shortcut and a per-POD-provider breakdown: heading 'Printify (1)' next to a 'Connect' button, meaning this teeinblue instance has NO active Printify account connection. The dialog still renders a full preview table (line item id, variant, SKU, fulfillment SKU, quantity, printareas with design thumbnail/key/width/height, status 'Ready', empty 'Fulfilled ID'), plus 'Fulfillment Shipping method: ---' and the shipping address, followed only by a 'Close' button — no visible submit/pay action was available while Printify shows 'Connect' instead of being connected. No network request to any Printify-related endpoint was observed as a result of this click (see network_observation_refs) — the two GraphQL calls around this time were read-only 'get' queries for orders_by_pk and order_item_activities, already used to populate the order-details page, not a fulfillment mutation. CONCLUSION: on an instance without a connected POD account, 'Confirm & Send to fulfill' is safely a dry-run/preview action that stops at a 'Connect Printify' prompt — it does not by itself submit a real production order or incur cost. This lowers the real-world risk of this action versus what was assumed before observing it, but connecting a REAL Printify account and re-attempting was explicitly out of scope for this run.

Opening the dropdown (menu opened only, NO option selected/clicked) shows 5 status options: Ready, Sent, Fulfilled, Paused, Canceled. This is presumably the manual override for tib_status independent of the automatic Printify/POD flow, letting a merchant mark an item Fulfilled/Canceled/Paused by hand. Not exercised further — selecting an option was out of scope to avoid an unintended state change with unknown side effects (e.g. possible outbound notification).
